video.title: The 2-minute walkthrough
video.caption: Where the platform stands today, what Phase 1 adds, and the road to finished.

today.label: Where it is today
today.headline: A working, audited prototype on a laptop.
built: 30 working screens: clinic and retail sign-up, coach, executive, partner and research views
A consent engine that enforces every toggle, plus deletion that issues a dated, printable certificate of what was erased
2,000 realistic test patients with simulated sleep histories
320 automated tests, all passing, and three outside AI code audits with every serious finding fixed
gaps: Runs on one laptop, with no web address or logins
Every patient is made up, and wearable data is simulated
The care assistant is scripted; no AI runs inside it yet
Too many screens for daily use

phases.name: Live & Real
phases.tagline: Real logins, real Garmin data from staff testers, Claude built in. No patients yet.

items.title: Live, with real logins
items.detail: A real web address with email sign-in and separate views for Kevin, coaches and staff, on a hosted database.

items.title: Garmin, through a data partner
items.detail: Testers connect their Garmin and each night syncs automatically, through a data partner that already has Garmin access. Partners like this also cover other brands that sync online, such as Fitbit and Oura. It can switch to a direct Garmin connection if Garmin reopens developer approvals.

items.title: One home screen per person
items.detail: Kevin sees five numbers and coaches see today's list. The research screens move behind an Advanced tab.

items.title: Staff pilot, scan to join
items.detail: Staff testers scan a QR code at the front desk, then consent and connect a watch from their own phone. Every screen shows what is real and what is simulated.

items.title: Phone sleep view
items.detail: Testers see their own nights on their phone, from an icon they add to their home screen. No app store download.

items.title: Ask your data
items.detail: Type a question, get a chart and a plain-English answer, with the query shown in plain words so Kevin can see what was counted.

items.title: Ask Sleeptopia from the Claude app
items.detail: A secure, read-only Sleeptopia connector in Kevin's own Claude account, on the web and on the phone. Ask by typing or out loud (dictation, or Claude's voice mode once it is tested with the connector). Every lookup it makes is logged. Staff-tester data appears there only as totals for the whole tester group, never a slice small enough to point to one person. Patient data stays out of it: a personal Claude account isn't covered by any HIPAA agreement, and even Anthropic's enterprise HIPAA agreement doesn't cover connectors.

items.title: Nightly AI research coordinator
items.detail: A scheduled Claude agent checks every tester's data each night, flags gaps, writes coach notes and sends Kevin a Monday status email.

items.title: Smart Care Assistant
items.detail: Claude replaces the scripted assistant. The same consent checks and clinical-escalation rules stay in front of it, every reply is checked against the existing safety rules, and new AI safety tests are added. Simulated patients and consenting staff testers only.

items.title: Sadie as the in-app guide
items.detail: The face from the website gives a short tour at first login and explains any screen on request.

items.title: Garmin obeys the consent kill switch
items.detail: A tester revokes consent, syncing stops, their data is deleted from Sleeptopia, the data partner is told to disconnect and delete it, and they get a deletion certificate with the real date. Proven on real wearable data.

items.title: Data-quality scorecard
items.detail: Nights received, missing nights and coverage for every tester, plus estimated wear time where the watch's data allows, so gaps are caught and fixed early.

items.title: This dashboard
items.detail: Every phase, milestone and decision with live status, in one place Kevin and Ben both use.

items.title: Hands-on session with Kevin's team
items.detail: Three people from Kevin's team use it hands-on. What trips them up gets fixed before Phase 1 closes.

items.title: Its own private code home
items.detail: The code moves to its own private repository. All tests and an outside AI code review run on every change.

exit: Kevin and Sleeptopia staff sign in from their own phones
At least 5 staff testers' Garmin nights sync on their own for 7 nights in a row after they connect
Questions Kevin picks up front get correct, hand-checked answers in the app and in Kevin's Claude app, and anything the privacy rules block is declined, never guessed
Revoking a tester's consent stops their sync and purges their data, with a certificate
Three of Kevin's team finish the hands-on session, and what they found is fixed
Every Phase 1 addition is shown working to Kevin, with Garmin as the wearable that must pass
Kevin signs off. Phase 1 closes and Phase 2 begins

phases.name: Ready for Real Patients
phases.tagline: The legal and security foundation, then the first 100 Sleeptopia patients.

items.title: HIPAA-ready hosting and agreements
items.detail: A host, database, AI provider and Garmin partner that each sign a HIPAA business associate agreement.

items.title: Research protocol and consent forms
items.detail: Drafted at the start of Phase 2, finalized by healthcare counsel and approved by a research review board (IRB).

items.title: Outside AI audit #4 on the live system
items.detail: AI red-team agents attack Sleeptopia's own logins, consent checks and Garmin connection. A written report and fixes follow.

items.title: First 25, then 100 real patients
items.detail: Coaches enroll Sleeptopia patients through the clinic door, with baseline nights captured before treatment.

items.title: CPAP and home sleep test data
items.detail: Therapy telemetry and sleep-test results flow in next to Garmin nights.

items.title: Direct Garmin connection
items.detail: Switch to Garmin's own data feed if Garmin reopens developer approvals and Sleeptopia's application clears.

items.title: Speed, accessibility and partner demo mode
items.detail: Every screen loads fast on a phone and passes accessibility checks. One switch shows a clean synthetic demo for partners.

items.title: Design system in Figma, linked to the code
items.detail: New screens are approved by Kevin as clickable prototypes before anything is built.

exit: Research review board approval and signed HIPAA agreements
100 consented patients with baseline nights captured
Consent revocation proven on live patient data

phases.name: Retail & the Positional Study
phases.tagline: The Mattress Hub door opens, and the flagship question gets its data.

items.title: In-store screener and mattress attach
items.detail: Shoppers take the sleep apnea screener in store; mattress purchases attach to consented records.

items.title: Under-mattress sensor cohort
items.detail: Nightly data from a sensor under the mattress, alongside Garmin, plus sleep position from a sensor picked because it reports position (most bed sensors don't).

items.title: Positional sleep apnea study launch
items.detail: Does mattress choice change outcomes for back-sleepers with apnea?

items.title: Native iPhone and Android apps
items.detail: Apple Health and Android health data join Garmin.

items.title: Oral appliance therapy arm
items.detail: Patients using oral appliances join the comparison, starting with partner dentists.

exit: Sensor cohort at twice the size the study needs

phases.name: Research & Revenue
phases.tagline: The data starts earning through research and partners, and powers personal recommendations.

items.title: De-identified research database
items.detail: Certified de-identified and released only under data-use agreements.

items.title: First abstract and methods paper
items.detail: Published credibility no competitor can buy.

items.title: Personal recommendations, version 1
items.detail: Designed to stay outside FDA medical-device rules: comfort tips, CPAP habit nudges and "talk to your provider" prompts, never a diagnosis or a therapy change, each type checked against FDA guidance before it ships.

items.title: Partner reporting and the first sponsored study
items.detail: Mattress makers, wearable companies and dental practices pay for insight, never for patient data.

items.title: Multi-site kit
items.detail: Other sleep and dental practices plug in and contribute data.

exit: Research database open under data-use agreements

garmin.text: Staff testers' Garmin nights, through a data partner with Garmin access
Patients' Garmin nights, under HIPAA agreements; direct Garmin if approvals reopen
Garmin plus under-mattress sensors power the positional study
Wearable and mattress partners sponsor studies on the de-identified data

complete.label: Complete
complete.sentence: A patient walks in through either door, is consented in plain language, has their sleep measured before and after treatment, and, pooled with a few thousand others, teaches us something worth publishing. A partner pays for those insights under a data-use agreement, and no identifiable patient data has ever been sold or leaked.
targets: 300 to 600 consented participants, growing to 1,500 to 3,000
At least one sponsored study and one outside site
Zero breaches; every use of identifiable patient data traces to a current consent
complete.kevinDefinition: Waiting on Kevin: a definition of success for the finished tool, in Kevin's own words. That answer sets the finish line; the sentence and targets above are Ben's draft.

updates.text: Phase 1 redefined as Live & Real: real logins, Garmin from staff testers, Claude built in. No patients until Phase 2.

Garmin has paused new developer applications, with no reopening date; existing integrations keep working. Phase 1 connects through a data partner that already has Garmin access, and a direct connection waits for Garmin to reopen.
The 2-minute walkthrough video is at the top of this page.
